basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 11.' and it opens 'Vers. 11. Germinet terra herbam virentem et lignum pomiferum. Omnia perfecta a Deo'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 11. Germinet terra herbam virentem et lignum pomiferum. Omnia perfecta a Deo cognita sunt. Unde homo in perfecta aetate creatus est, et arbores cum foliis suis simul et fructu. Hinc et lignum pomiferum dicit habens unumquodque sementem. | Haec sementis est frugum et arborum: semen vero hominum, et animalium seminium vel sementum exordium cujuscunque rei.
